problems.title: The printed covariance conditions permit a negative class gradient
problems.source_location: Theorem 3.2, Eqs.(3)–(5), PDF p.5; Appendix B.4, PDF pp.26–27
claim: The theorem gives nonnegative class-weight gradient when \(\sigma^2\ge\|b\|^2/(4d_{\rm irr})\) and \(\sigma^2\ge\|c\|^2/(4d_{\rm noise})\), where \(c=\operatorname{Cov}(v^{\rm noise},\hat y)\) already includes noise severity.
analysis: Let \(Y,R_0,R_1,R_2,R_3\) be independent uniform signs, \(y=(Y+1)/2\), \[v=(Y,R_0,0,R_1/2,R_2/2,R_3/2)\], \(\mu=1\), \(s=1/2\), and all weights \(1\). Use opposite unit text embeddings in direction \((11/10,0,0,8,4,2)\). Then \(\hat y=\mathbf1\{(11/10)Y+4R_1+2R_2+R_3>0\}\), with strict margin \(0.1\). All \(32\) atoms have norm squared \(11/4\). Their exact moments are \(p=1/2\), \(C=8\), \(\sigma=1/16\), \(b=0\), and \(c=(3/16,1/16,1/16)\). Both printed conditions hold because \(1/256\ge11/3072\). Varying only the class weight \(x\), the retained variance identity gives \[V(x)=\frac{4x^2+11}{64x^2+112},\qquad V^{\prime}(1)=-\frac2{121}.\] The printed derivative instead gives \(5/242>0\).
result: The sign conclusion fails under the stated model. At \(s=1\) the missing factor disappears, and for \(s\ge1\) the printed condition can still suffice. The paper does not impose that restriction on its latent severity. A full update’s accuracy and the autodifferentiated release objective are separate questions.
repair: The noise bracket must be \(4\sigma^2s^2d_{\rm noise}-\|c\|^2\), giving sufficient condition \(\sigma^2\ge\|c\|^2/(4s^2d_{\rm noise})\) for positive severity/dimension. Quotient differentiation also gives shift derivative \(-2V(\mathbf1)s^2\delta^2/D_0\); its nonpositive sign survives the coefficient correction. Zero severity or absent components need separate omission rather than division by zero.
